comment: Positions the validation schemas type as plain strings or plain maps but that the specification gives a meaning the resolver needs. Each entry names the versions it holds for, the generated state, the position inside it (at: a member path, * for every item or member) or its member names (keys), what the position is, and why. tools/object-model.cjs refuses an entry without a reason and an entry whose position the generated model does not have, so the overlay cannot outlive the schemas it corrects.

entries.reason: A Link's operationRef is a URI reference to an Operation Object, which the resolver resolves and checks but never substitutes (the Link Object).
A Link's operationId names an Operation by its operationId, an implicit connection (the Link Object).
An Operation's tags name Tag Objects by name, an implicit connection; a tag no Tag Object declares is allowed and reported (the Operation Object).
A 3.2 Tag's parent names another Tag by name, and the chain of parents must not loop (the 3.2 Tag Object).
A Discriminator mapping value is a schema name or a URI reference to a schema, told apart as the Discriminator Object says: a locator, never substituted.
A 3.2 Discriminator's defaultMapping is read as a mapping value is (the 3.2 Discriminator Object).
A Security Requirement's member names name Security Schemes, in 3.2 by name or by URI reference; its values are scope lists, data (the Security Requirement Object).
